introduction_markdown:
Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, Ordinary Level Examination, June 2020. Chemistry, Paper 2 (subject code 0515). Duration: two and a half hours.

This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: attempt ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 questions answered. Section B: answer BOTH questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3.

In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Cu = 64.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the following table and complete the information needed.

| No | TEST PROCEDURE | OBSERVATION | INFERENCE | Marks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (i) | To $2\ \text{cm}^3$ of solution A is added 5 drops of NaOH(aq) warmed | A colourless pungent gas is evolved. The gas turns damp red litmus paper blue |  | 2 marks |
| (ii) | To $2\ \text{cm}^3$ of solution A is added 2 drops of $\mathrm{BaCl_2}$(aq) followed by dil HCl(aq) |  | Presence of $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$ ions | 2 marks |
| (iii) | To $2\ \text{cm}^3$ of solution B is added 2 drops of NaOH(aq) | Dirty-green precipitate is formed |  | 1 mark |
| (iv) | To $2\ \text{cm}^3$ of solution B is added a few drops of $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ followed by dil $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ | A white precipitate is formed |  | 1 mark |
| (v) |  | X gives a brick red flame colour |  | 3 marks |
| (vi) | A solid sample of X strongly heated in a test tube | A brown gas is evolved |  | 2 marks |
questions.corrige_markdown:
| No | TEST PROCEDURE | OBSERVATION | INFERENCE |
|---|---|---|---|
| (i) | NaOH(aq) added to A and warmed | Colourless pungent gas turns damp red litmus paper blue | The gas is **ammonia**, $\mathrm{NH_3}$: A contains **ammonium ions**, $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ |
| (ii) | $\mathrm{BaCl_2}$(aq) then dil HCl added to A | **White precipitate** ($\mathrm{BaSO_4}$) that is **insoluble in dil HCl** | Presence of $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$ ions |
| (iii) | NaOH(aq) added to B | Dirty-green precipitate | **$\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ ions** present (the precipitate is $\mathrm{Fe(OH)_2}$) |
| (iv) | $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ then dil $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ added to B | White precipitate | **$\mathrm{Cl^-}$ ions** present (the precipitate is AgCl) |
| (v) | **Flame test:** a clean nichrome or platinum wire is dipped in concentrated HCl, then in solid X (or its solution), and held in a non-luminous Bunsen flame | Brick red flame | **$\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$ ions** present |
| (vi) | Solid X strongly heated | Brown gas ($\mathrm{NO_2}$) evolved | **$\mathrm{NO_3^-}$ ions** present: X is a nitrate |

Useful equations: $\mathrm{NH_4^+} + \mathrm{OH^-} \rightarrow \mathrm{NH_3} + \mathrm{H_2O}$; $\mathrm{Ba^{2+}} + \mathrm{SO_4^{2-}} \rightarrow \mathrm{BaSO_4}$; $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}} + 2\mathrm{OH^-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe(OH)_2}$; $\mathrm{Ag^+} + \mathrm{Cl^-} \rightarrow \mathrm{AgCl}$; $2\mathrm{Ca(NO_3)_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CaO} + 4\mathrm{NO_2} + \mathrm{O_2}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give the chemical identity of A, B, and X.

A: ...

B: ...

X: ... *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
- **A:** ammonium sulphate, $(\mathrm{NH_4})_2\mathrm{SO_4}$ (contains $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ and $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$).
- **B:** iron(II) chloride, $\mathrm{FeCl_2}$ (contains $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Cl^-}$).
- **X:** calcium nitrate, $\mathrm{Ca(NO_3)_2}$ (contains $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{NO_3^-}$).

questions.enonce_markdown:
In order to determine the chemical formula of an oxide of copper, a student passed dry hydrogen gas through copper oxide in a porcelain boat in a hard glass tube.

The following results were obtained:

- Mass of empty boat = 14.4 g
- Mass of boat and of copper oxide sample before heating = 18.4 g
- Mass of boat + sample at the end of experiment = 17.6

Determine the Empirical formula of the oxide of copper. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Hydrogen removes the oxygen from the copper oxide, leaving copper: copper oxide $+ \mathrm{H_2} \rightarrow$ copper $+ \mathrm{H_2O}$.

- Mass of copper oxide $= 18.4 - 14.4 = 4.0$ g.
- Mass of copper left $= 17.6 - 14.4 = 3.2$ g.
- Mass of oxygen removed $= 18.4 - 17.6 = 0.8$ g (check: $3.2 + 0.8 = 4.0$ g).

| | Cu | O |
|---|---|---|
| Mass (g) | 3.2 | 0.8 |
| Moles ($\text{mass}/A_r$) | $3.2/64 = 0.05$ | $0.8/16 = 0.05$ |
| Ratio (divide by 0.05) | 1 | 1 |

The empirical formula is **CuO**.

(The unit of the last mass is not printed in the question; grams are assumed.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Why is it advisable to wear eye goggles when working in the laboratory? *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: To **protect the eyes** from splashes of corrosive or harmful chemicals, from flying fragments of hot or broken glass, and from irritating fumes.
